title.en: Professional Scrum Master (PSM I) Practice Assessment — Red Tangerine

description.en: Twenty practice-assessment questions transcribed from the supplied result screenshot. The original answer options, correct-answer markings and available grey-box explanations are preserved.

question.en: #1. Which of the following are part of the Scrum framework?

options.text: Velocity
User Stories
Story Points
Definition of Ready
None of the above

explanation.en: Scrum is a lightweight framework with various processes, techniques and methods that can be employed within the framework, such as the use of user stories and story points.

question.en: #2. What is the purpose of Sprint 0?

cards.correctAnswer: There is no such thing as Sprint 0 in Scrum

options.text: For the Scrum Team to produce the first version of the ordered, sized Product Backlog
For the Developers to carry out a feasibility analysis of the requirements so that they can plan and estimate more accurately
For the Product Owner to build a business case that demonstrates the return on investment for the product development
There is no such thing as Sprint 0 in Scrum

question.en: #3. What place does Project Management have in Scrum?

cards.correctAnswer: Although no role of Project Manager is recognised in Scrum, Project Management skills may be needed by the Scrum Team, and the competencies may be carried out by Scrum Masters, Developers or Product Owners

options.text: Scrum does not recognise Project Managers; Project Management skills and the Project Manager role is obsolete

Although no role of Project Manager is recognised in Scrum, Project Management skills may be needed by the Scrum Team, and the competencies may be carried out by Scrum Masters, Developers or Product Owners

Project Managers are required in a separate PMO function. They create the Sprint by Sprint plan, the end of Sprint report, and ensure that the Scrum Master, Developers and Product Owner are fulfilling their duties
The Scrum Master is an Agile Project Manager

question.en: #4. Scrum Masters are described as “True Leaders”. What does this mean?

cards.correctAnswer: They lead by serving the needs of the Scrum Team and the larger organisation

options.text: They lead by serving the needs of the Scrum Team and the larger organisation
The entire organisation must respect their decisions
They lead all of the Scrum events
They are ultimately accountable for the success of Scrum implementations and the success of products

question.en: #5. If a product has been delivered according to the originally planned timelines, within budget and all “must have scope” delivered, it can be deemed a success.

options.text: True
False

explanation.en: Meeting customer’s and user’s needs, their desired outcomes and solving their problems in a way that results in an overall positive impact for the organisation is a far better measure of success.

question.en: #6. When is the Increment released?

cards.correctAnswer: As soon as a Product Backlog item meets the Definition of Done, an Increment is born and the decision to release it can be made

options.text: After it has been reviewed and signed off as “Done” in the Sprint Review
Following the user acceptance testing phase that follows the Sprint after the Increment was Done
As soon as a Product Backlog item meets the Definition of Done, an Increment is born and the decision to release it can be made
The decision to release an Increment is at the sole discretion of the Product Owner, regardless of the state of the Increment

explanation.en: Multiple Increments may be created and released during a Sprint. The Sprint Review should never be considered as a gate to releasing value. For an Increment to be releasable it must meet the Definition of Done.

question.en: #7. Should the Product Owner attend the Sprint Retrospective?

cards.correctAnswer: Yes – they are part of the Scrum Team

options.text: Yes – they are part of the Scrum Team
No – their presence might result in the rest of the Scrum Team being uncomfortable in being open about their challenges, thus transparency is reduced
It is up to the Developers to decide

explanation.en: The Product Owner is part of the Scrum Team and as such shares in the Scrum Team’s successes, shortcomings and improvement actions. If the Developers are uncomfortable with the Product Owner being in the Sprint Retrospective, this should be considered as an impediment to be resolved.

question.en: #8. The ideal Scrum Team is one that is;

cards.correctAnswer: Cross-functional, meaning that it has all of the skills needed to turn Product Backlog items into Done Increments on the team

options.text: Cross-functional, meaning that it has all of the skills needed to turn Product Backlog items into Done Increments on the team
Made up of a Scrum Master, a Product Owner, a Business Analyst and one tester for every programmer
Fully trained and experts in Scrum theory
Made up of team members that get on with the job and do not moan about “impediments slowing them down”

question.en: #9. Why should an organisation adopt Scrum?

cards.correctAnswer: To manage complexity, maximize value, optimize predictability and control risk

options.text: To increase speed, productivity and efficiency
To manage complexity, maximize value, optimize predictability and control risk
To deliver project scope, on-time and within budget
To eliminate complexity, maximise throughput and reduce costs

explanation.en: From the Scrum Guide… “Scrum employs an iterative, incremental approach to optimize predictability and to control risk”.

question.en: #10. When there is a lot of uncertainty, for example about user needs, market potential, viability of the solution, the best way to proceed is to;

cards.correctAnswer: Collaborate as a Scrum Team on how to learn and reduce risk as quickly as possible while still producing a “Done”, valuable, usable Increment each Sprint

options.text: Postpone sprinting while further analysis is carried out and a more comprehensive design is created
Collaborate as a Scrum Team on how to learn and reduce risk as quickly as possible while still producing a “Done”, valuable, usable Increment each Sprint
Keep a risk register and assign the Scrum Master to manage it
Have the Product Owner make a decision about what to do, so that resources are kept utilised

explanation.en: Scrum is designed for complex, uncertain environments. The regular cadence of Sprints and the feedback loops given by the Scrum events enable iterative and incremental learning, enabling options for how to proceed to emerge.

question.en: #11. Why is Product Backlog refinement not a Scrum event?

cards.correctAnswer: Scrum does not prescribe a method, regular cadence, attendees or timebox for how Scrum Teams carry out Product Backlog refinement

options.text: Scrum does not prescribe a method, regular cadence, attendees or timebox for how Scrum Teams carry out Product Backlog refinement
Product Backlog refinement is part of the Sprint Planning event
Having six events in Scrum is too many for most people to remember
Product Backlog refinement is a Scrum event

question.en: #12. During a Sprint, the Developers determine that they will not be able to complete all of the items forecasted. What should the Scrum Team do?

cards.correctAnswer: Renegotiate the scope, with a focus on how to still meet the Sprint Goal

options.text: Renegotiate the scope, with a focus on how to still meet the Sprint Goal
The Developers should swarm on the items most likely to be finished so that there is something to show at the Sprint Review
Abandon the current Sprint and start a new one
Skip testing, and catch up with it in the next Sprint
Drop the Sprint Retrospective and Daily Scrum so that the Developers have more time to get the work done

explanation.en: During the Sprint, scope may be negotiated between the Developers and Product Owner as more is learned.

question.en: #13. Which of the following might be consequences of having product teams that are given features to deliver/implement?

correctAnswer: Potential creativity and innovation residing in the team is wasted
The team could potentially come up with better solutions to the problems to be solved
Team members may feel less autonomy, mastery and purpose with regards to their work
Teams might end up being measured and judged on output rather than outcomes

options.text: Potential creativity and innovation residing in the team is wasted
The team could potentially come up with better solutions to the problems to be solved
Team members may feel less autonomy, mastery and purpose with regards to their work
Teams might end up being measured and judged on output rather than outcomes

question.en: #14. Mature Scrum Teams can drop certain elements of Scrum such as the Daily Scrum and Sprint Retrospective when they feel they no longer add value

options.text: True
False

explanation.en: The Scrum Framework is immutable, while implementing parts of Scrum is possible, the result is not Scrum. Dropping Scrum events results in lost opportunities for inspection and adaptation and reduces transparency.

question.en: #15. How should the Sprint Backlog be ordered?

cards.correctAnswer: Scrum does not prescribe ordering of the Sprint Backlog

options.text: Scrum does not prescribe ordering of the Sprint Backlog
The ordering of Product Backlog items on the Sprint Backlog should be the same as they were when they were on the Product Backlog
By whatever the Developers say
By whatever the Product Owner says

question.en: #16. How can a Scrum Team best improve its defect rate?

cards.correctAnswer: Test automation, peer review, gathering earlier feedback, getting closer to the end user are just a few options that the Scrum Team could try

options.text: Replace some of the team members with testing specialists
Introduce a hardening Sprint where the entire focus on the Sprint is spent on finding and fixing bugs
Introduce a “Definition of Ready” with rigorous criteria which ensures all requirements are captured in detail before the Developers start the work
Inspect the Definition of Done and make individual team members accountable for ensuring that different parts are fulfilled
Test automation, peer review, gathering earlier feedback, getting closer to the end user are just a few options that the Scrum Team could try

explanation.en: Defects are not just bugs in the product. A defect is anything that reduces the value of the product to a customer, user, or to the organization itself. Defects are generally things that don’t work as intended.

question.en: #17. Which of the following should be considered when crafting an effective goal?

cards.correctAnswer: It expresses a measurable desired outcome

options.text: Ensuring that it has a deadline for delivery
The exact scope that needs to be delivered is clear
It expresses a measurable desired outcome
It includes a projection of revenue increase when the goal is met

question.en: #18. Who monitors the progress of work during a Sprint?

options.text: The Scrum Master
The Product Owner
The Project Manager
The Lead Developer
None of the above

explanation.en: The Developers are accountable for managing, executing and monitoring the plan for the Sprint. This plan is made transparent in the Sprint Backlog.

question.en: #19. Stakeholders cannot agree on which product and feature ideas to focus on. Which of the following is most aligned with Scrum theory in how to proceed?

cards.correctAnswer: Take an empirical approach and test the value propositions of each, either through small experiments which may involve building small parts of functionality and gathering feedback

options.text: Take an empirical approach and test the value propositions of each, either through small experiments which may involve building small parts of functionality and gathering feedback
The Product Owner should decide based on their intuition and make a presentation to the stakeholders to justify their decisions
Escalate the impasse to higher management for a decision to be made at executive level
Use a weighted job short calculation and go with whatever the result is

question.en: #20. Scrum Teams that focus on output and not outcomes may not be exhibiting which element of Scrum?

cards.correctAnswer: The Scrum value of courage to work on the right thing

options.text: Achieving the highest possible velocity
The Scrum value of courage to work on the right thing
Reaching the optimal “performing” state as a team
Celebrating what was achieved in the Sprint Review
